- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward — true values often dip below forecast peak.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, suggesting a lag in recognizing downward momentum.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when recent history includes strong upward moves.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the short term — true values often return to prior levels faster than forecast suggests.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the middle of the horizon, especially when historical volatility is low.
- Model does not adjust for recent downward trends — it continues to project upward momentum even when data shows weakening demand or supply constraints.
